video_title: Media Availability: Brian Keefe, Tre Johnson, and Will Riley | 10.10.26

quotes.speaker: Brian Keefe
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Keefe on the Wizards' ongoing development and team chemistry
quotes.excerpt: we're learning about our team and we're growing
quotes.quote: I talked about we're learning about our team and we're growing. We had some really good positive moments out there. Obviously, start the game the defense and then you can see us. I think we had 21 fast break points in the first half. We can rebound and get stops and get on transition, really good offense is coming. That's going to be a work in progress. We're learning how to play with each other. Some stuff entering offense needs to get better, but that's why we're out there in the preseason.
quotes.social_post: Brian Keefe says the Wizards are still a work in progress as they learn to play together. He noted that while the offense needs improvement, the team is focused on building chemistry through the preseason.

quotes.speaker: Brian Keefe
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Keefe on Alex Sarr's defensive impact and chemistry with AD
quotes.excerpt: the impact we had defensively, being able to protect the rim, roam around, help each other
quotes.quote: I think you saw at the start of the game the impact we had defensively, being able to protect the rim, roam around, help each other. And then he saw the connection. AD I think hit him in the second half for a corner three. So some good chemistry things we saw out there, but nice to see Alex back in action.
quotes.social_post: Brian Keefe liked what he saw from Alex Sarr in his return to action. He highlighted the defensive impact and the growing chemistry between Sarr and Anthony Davis.

quotes.speaker: Brian Keefe
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Keefe on Justin Champagnie's versatility and fourth-quarter impact
quotes.excerpt: we're looking to see different combos, who plays well together
quotes.quote: That's what I talked about the other day. We're looking to see different combos, who plays well together. You're going to see that the next couple of games too. Justin was going to get in the second half tonight and start the fourth quarter. Obviously, he had a great impact in there in overtime.
quotes.social_post: Brian Keefe is using the preseason to experiment with different lineup combinations. He praised Justin Champagnie for his impact during the fourth quarter and overtime.

quotes.speaker: Brian Keefe
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Keefe on Trey Johnson's defensive growth and playmaking
quotes.excerpt: his defense is improving, his secondary playmaking is improving
quotes.quote: You see the improvements on the defensive end. I loved he just catched and shot it today. In that start with our defense, we were out in transition, our guys look for him. We know the type of shooter he is. Trey Young did a great job of finding him in transition and kicking that ball ahead to him. That's why he's here. He's here to make shots, but his defense is improving, his secondary playmaking is improving. He's had a good summer.
quotes.social_post: Brian Keefe is seeing growth from Tre Johnson. He praised the young guard for his defensive improvements and secondary playmaking ability during the summer.

quotes.speaker: Brian Keefe
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Keefe on the team's spacing and chemistry in the preseason
quotes.excerpt: the combinations of who's playing, how they're going to play together
quotes.quote: That's the stuff that's going to take some time, the combinations of who's playing, how they're going to play together. But you can see our defensive impact. The offense is going to take some time. These guys, some of these guys have never played together. We're playing two bigs, they're learning how to space off each other. I think we showed some moments of growth, but you also saw the physicality part of that too.
quotes.social_post: Brian Keefe acknowledges that the Wizards' offense will take time to gel. He noted that playing two bigs requires learning how to space the floor effectively.

quotes.speaker: Tre Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Tre Johnson on the importance of team unselfishness and ball movement
quotes.excerpt: it's been great having almost anybody who gets the rebound can push it
quotes.quote: It's been great having almost anybody who gets the rebound can push it. We just all got to run. Make sure get the rebound first, of course, but then yeah just running. Running to our spots and having good spacing.
quotes.social_post: Tre Johnson emphasizes the importance of pace for the Wizards. He says the team is focused on running to their spots and maintaining good spacing after securing rebounds.

quotes.speaker: Tre Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Tre Johnson on building chemistry with teammates on the court
quotes.excerpt: it's like a two-way street we're both figuring each other out
quotes.quote: I feel like it's like a two-way street we're both figuring each other out. So like the dropping it behind the back, he probably obviously saw me and Bud doing that so in that same situation, it was easy for me to pick up on that. But I feel like we both just figuring each other out, especially running the court and stuff like that. So I feel like just the more games we play it's going to be better.
quotes.social_post: Tre Johnson says building chemistry is a two-way street. He believes the more games the team plays together, the better they will get at reading each other on the court.

quotes.speaker: Tre Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Tre Johnson on the team's defensive identity and physicality
quotes.excerpt: we think we could be more physical and more better at it
quotes.quote: We for sure, the guys that were here last year, we for sure dealt with that like a lot everywhere we went. And so when we kind of implemented that in our defense and our scheme and how we wanted to play, we enjoyed that. And especially doing it in practice against each other and then bringing it out to the game. We think we could be more physical and more better at it, so we're still just working on it.
quotes.social_post: Tre Johnson says the Wizards are looking to establish a more physical defensive identity this season. He noted that the team is working hard to implement that scheme in practice.

quotes.speaker: Tre Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Tre Johnson on his offseason focus on strength and defense
quotes.excerpt: my first thing I worked on was like getting stronger, putting on more weight
quotes.quote: My first thing I worked on was like getting stronger, putting on more weight. That was probably the first and biggest thing. Defense, I worked on it like a little bit, but I feel like defense is just like a one-two thing. I had to shift my mentality towards that just because I want to be on the court for as long as possible and I didn't want to let defense be like the reason to keep me off.
quotes.social_post: Tre Johnson says his main offseason focus was getting stronger. He also shifted his mentality toward defense, noting he wants to ensure he stays on the court as much as possible.

quotes.speaker: Tre Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Tre Johnson on the value of defensive mentors like Anthony Davis
quotes.excerpt: it's for sure been a lot of help, especially like the new addition with the big guys
quotes.quote: It's for sure been a lot of help, especially like the new addition with the big guys because they got different styles and different things that they like. So just talking to them, knowing who you're in the game with and kind of just trying to adjust on the fly. Like Anthony Davis don't like when you in his way and he trying to block a shot, so you got to get out of the way.
quotes.social_post: Tre Johnson is learning from the Wizards' big men. He joked about the importance of knowing where to be, saying Anthony Davis does not like it when you get in his way while he is trying to block a shot.

quotes.speaker: Tre Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Tre Johnson on the team's depth and defensive requirements
quotes.excerpt: the team is too deep, you have to play defense
quotes.quote: The team is too deep, everybody can play offense. Like everybody sitting on that bench can play offense. You got to play defense if you're trying to play. That's the only way you're going to stay out. The team is too deep, you have to play defense.
quotes.social_post: Tre Johnson is clear on the rotation requirements for this deep Wizards roster. You have to play defense if you are trying to play. The team is too deep, you have to play defense.

quotes.speaker: Will Riley
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Riley on the team's spacing and defensive performance
quotes.excerpt: guys were just spacing the floor well, we were moving the ball so well
quotes.quote: It felt good, you know. It was good to, you know, get a feel back and, you know, guys were just spacing the floor well, we were moving the ball so well and guys were just hitting shots. And especially on defensive end, I feel like we were getting good stops and just playing fast, so I feel like that's what helped translate buckets.
quotes.social_post: Will Riley felt good about the team's performance, highlighting the ball movement and defensive stops that helped the Wizards play fast and translate that into buckets.

quotes.speaker: Will Riley
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Riley on the team's offensive growth and spacing
quotes.excerpt: we're so big that it's very hard to guard
quotes.quote: I mean you saw like the first quarter like the guys were just, it was just flowing. Guys were moving so fast, just playing the right size. We're so big that it's very hard to guard, especially like just the amount of size we have on the offensive end and the defensive end, it's hard to stop.
quotes.social_post: Will Riley believes the Wizards' size is a major advantage. He noted that the team's length makes them very difficult to guard on both ends of the floor.

quotes.speaker: Will Riley
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Riley on molding his game around team defensive needs
quotes.excerpt: defense is what's going to keep you on the court at the end of the day
quotes.quote: For sure, you know, that defense is what's going to keep you on the court at the end of the day. So, you know, really locking on that. Like Tre Johnson said, we got so many talented guys, like it's like if you look at the stats, down the line, everyone's scoring. It's just simple for everybody, I feel like. We got a lot of stars, so it's like, like I said, defensive end is really what the key is for this team.
quotes.social_post: Will Riley echoes the sentiment that defense is the key to playing time. With so many talented scorers on the roster, he believes the defensive end is what will define this team.

quotes.speaker: Will Riley
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Riley on the impact of his physical development
quotes.excerpt: it's definitely helping on the defensive end and, you know, just helping me like stand my ground
quotes.quote: It's definitely helping on the defensive end and, you know, just helping me like stand my ground, like especially just dribbling the ball, guys pressuring and stuff like that. Just little things like that, I feel like it definitely helps.
quotes.social_post: Will Riley says his physical development is helping him on the defensive end. He noted that being stronger helps him stand his ground when handling pressure.

quotes.speaker: Will Riley
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Riley on his evolving leadership role on the team
quotes.excerpt: me and JC, we had a lot of years or I have one year, but he has a lot of years
quotes.quote: Yeah, I mean, you know, I feel like me and JC, we had a lot of years or I have one year, but he has a lot of years. And, you know, I feel like we we definitely, you know, helped in our leadership role at the end there. And, yeah, those guys were there, playing phenomenal, whether it was like Reese, you know, picking up full court, he's amazing defender, Felix at the basket, you know, I don't know how long his wingspan is, 7'100 or whatever it is, but he he was blocking everything. And, you know, Chris Livingston, obviously, you know, freak athlete, he was getting everything and JC just sniper.
quotes.social_post: Will Riley is embracing a leadership role. He praised his teammates for their defensive efforts, specifically highlighting the defensive intensity from players like Reese and Felix.

quotes.speaker: Will Riley
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Riley on playing within the flow of the offense
quotes.excerpt: we were just playing in the flow of the offense to be honest
quotes.quote: I wouldn't say necessarily there was anything I was trying to work on. I feel like I was just, we were just playing in the flow of the offense to be honest and, you know, the ball was finding me, it was finding it was finding everybody, it was just moving. So, you know, it was it was fun basketball to play.
quotes.social_post: Will Riley says the Wizards are focused on playing within the flow of the offense. He noted that the ball is moving well and finding everyone on the court.

quotes.speaker: Will Riley
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Riley on the benefits of playing with multiple bigs
quotes.excerpt: on the defensive end, it's no-brainer, it's so easy
quotes.quote: On the defensive end, it's no-brainer, it's so easy. Just pressure guys, force them to force them into the bigs. They're they'll block everything. And then on the offensive end, it's very hard to guard because, you know, there's going to be a mismatch somewhere unless they have two bigs as well and then it's also going to be a mismatch. So it's I feel like it's it's good for us on both ends.
quotes.social_post: Will Riley sees the benefit of playing with multiple bigs. He says it makes defense easier by forcing opponents into the rim protectors and creates constant mismatches on offense.
